ModMetaData.name: AgentTouchFix
ModMetaData.author: SleepSheepQwQ
ModMetaData.description:
Runtime Harmony fixes for the Android touch port (Waylith engine), no vanilla DLL is modified.
1) Developer tools (LudeonTK DebugTools) work with touch. The port turns every map tap into a synthetic selection (PortUI.MobileSelectionController.Tap) and never produces the MouseDown that DebugTool.DebugToolOnGUI needs, so an armed tool never fires and the tap is stolen by the selector. - PortUI.MobileSelectionController.Tap is skipped while a tool is armed; the tool's clickAction is invoked instead, with UI.MouseCell() and UI.MouseMapPosition() pinned to the tapped target. - The tap is snapped through PortUI's own candidate picker (MobileSelectionController.Candidates: the exact cell first, then the 5x5 surrounding cells within a 28.8 px screen radius, nearest first), so a tap does not have to land exactly on the entity. Empty ground keeps the raw tap coordinate, unrounded. - Long press cancels the armed tool (touch equivalent of the right mouse button). - RimWorld.Selector.HandleMapClicks is skipped while a tool is armed (real mouse fallback) and a half-open drag box is disarmed so selection can never "stick". - LudeonTK.DebugTool.DebugToolOnGUI is suppressed on the frame a tool already fired through the touch path, so a real mouse event cannot fire the same tool twice.
2) Pointer no longer sticks after a two finger gesture, and a one finger drag no longer turns into a zoom. - Ports1de.TouchGestureEngine.SecondUp leaves state = Ignore and no branch of Move()/Up() handles Ignore, so the finger still on the screen emits nothing until it is lifted and pressed again. The postfix forces state = Idle and drops the pinch baseline / inertia. - RwHost.TouchControls.OnTouch: on ACTION_POINTER_UP / ACTION_CANCEL the engine and the GameCamera accumulators are reset, and the remaining finger is re-armed as a pan (or the remaining two fingers as a pinch) so the gesture continues instead of dying. - Stale GameCamera pan/zoom accumulators are cleared at gesture end, which removes the "leftover zoom applied on the next frame" effect.
3) Silent by default (v5). Nothing is written to the in-game log window, so the game no longer pops the "there were errors / warnings" dialog. - Every line goes to files/game/agenttouchfix.log (last 512 KB per session kept). - Optional diagnostics: create an empty file files/game/agenttouchfix.diag next to it and restart. The touch/camera diagnostics are then re-enabled and INFO lines are additionally mirrored to the in-game console (Log.Message only - never Warning/Error). Delete the file to go quiet again. The flag is read once, at startup. - Runtime failures (a tap or a gesture) are file-only; only a patch that fails to apply at startup reports once, in game.
4) Snapping is hit tested (v6). A tapped map position is only snapped onto a Thing when the tap really aimed at it: inside the thing's own footprint, or within 16 dp (and never more than half a cell) of its projected screen position. A tap on empty ground next to an item now stays on the empty cell, which is what terrain / spawn tools need. With nothing under the tap and a single thing selected, the selected thing is used instead (tools that answer to the selection). Switch (read once at startup), files/game/agenttouchfix.snap: auto (default, also used when the file is absent) - the hit test above always - old behaviour: snap to the nearest candidate no matter how far the tap was off - never snap; the exact tapped cell and position are used
5) Tooltips no longer stick to the touch point (v6). The port parks the cursor on the last tap, so Verse.TooltipHandler sees Mouse.IsOver(rect) forever and re-opens the hover text over the button labels. TooltipHandler.TipRegion / TipRegionByKey are now skipped while a touch is in progress: no tooltip for 1.5 s after a tap (and as long as the pointer stays parked on the tap point), but holding the finger down for 600 ms or more shows the description on purpose. On desktop, or with a real mouse being moved, nothing changes. A skipped tooltip never calls Event.current.Use().
6) Textures stop blinking / turning grey after a memory pressure event (v7). RwHost.AndroidMemoryAndGcGovernor answered one pressure event twice: GameBoundary released every decoded texture staging buffer and set renderTrim = 1, then RenderBoundary released them again on the next render frame - exactly when the queued uploads are consumed - so the buffers that were decoded but not yet uploaded were evicted and the texture showed as a grey block until it was decoded again. The render-side release is now skipped within 500 ms of a game-side one. renderTrim is left set, so that trim is deferred to a later frame instead of being lost; pause, surface and device-loss paths are untouched.
7) Double tapping a building selects every one of that kind on screen (v7). PortUI.MobileSelectionController.Tap only had a multi-select branch for ThingCategory.Item, so a double tap on a wall or a workbench just re-selected the single building. A second tap on the same building within 400 ms is now handled by the mod: it pins UI.MouseCell()/UI.MouseMapPosition() to the building and calls the vanilla Selector.SelectAllMatchingObjectUnderMouseOnScreen(), which is what a desktop double click does. The current selection is not cleared first.
8) Text typed with the Android keyboard is no longer dropped, which is what made Chinese input look broken (v7). Ports1de.TextEditMailbox.TryTake() compared the whole TextEditTarget - window id, keyboard control id and the field rect - so any layout change between opening the editor and the IME answering (a scrolled window, a re-laid-out dialog, the keyboard resizing the screen) threw the text away. When the exact match fails, a pending answer from the same window is delivered instead: exactly once, and only if it has not expired. Both sides must report the same window id, and when there is no window at all (id -1) the keyboard control id has to match as well.
9) Mouse buttons and keys are released when the app loses the input device (v8). The host forwards input to the engine and keeps its own mirror of what is held, but it clears that mirror on surface destroy, configuration change and focus loss without forwarding a release - and OnPause does not even clear it - so the engine kept a button pressed whose release was never sent (the mirror and the engine then agree on "nothing is held", and no later event ever corrects it). The same lifecycle events now release every held mouse button first. OnPause also resets the mirror, which that method never did, so the next press is not swallowed. Keyboard pushes had no bookkeeping at all, so a held key (WASD, Shift) stayed down after focus loss / pause / surface recreation and the pawn kept walking. Presses are now tracked by scan code and the missing releases are sent from the same four lifecycle methods. KEYCODE_BACK is not tracked: it maps to Escape and OnBackPressed already sends its own press+release pair.
10) Lifting one mouse button no longer releases the others (v8). RwHost clears every held button whenever an ACTION_UP arrives. On devices that report the still held buttons in that event, a button the player never released was let go, and the following move event pressed it again - a phantom click / a broken drag. Now only the button that actually went up is released, exactly as the port already does for a second button on a pointer-up; the ordinary single button release is handled by the unmodified game code.
11) Memory is now handed back when the app goes to the background (v8). TRIM_MEMORY_UI_HIDDEN (20) was the only pressure level the port ignored, even though it is the one Android sends when the activity leaves the screen. It is now answered the same way as TRIM_MEMORY_BACKGROUND (40): the texture buffers are released at the next game boundary, at most once every 5 seconds.
Everything is registered with AccessTools and fails soft: a missing target is recorded in the log file and the rest of the patches stay active. Nothing is patched permanently outside these methods.
Requires the mobile port (PortUI/RwHost present). Harmless on desktop RimWorld: the touch-only patches are simply skipped.
